newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -Norwich Union makes active debut.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -Norwich Union makes active debut.

text.p: Newly quoted insurer Norwich Union Plc attracted mixed trading in the UK stock options on Monday as the shares made their stock market debut, dealers said.

The biggest deal by early afternoon was a long straddle in which 375 June 330 puts and calls were bought at 10p each. The straddle will be in profit if the underlying share is either below 310p or above 350p by expiry on Wednesday, June 18.
Elsewhere in Norwich options, another dealer bought 200 June 330 calls at 9-1/2p while a separate trader sold 200 June 330 puts at 9p.
By 1300 GMT, the shares were at 329p or up 39p, compared with the public offer price of 290p.

A ratioed short cylinder was the main deal in tobacco-to-insurance group BAT Industries Plc in which around 400,000 shares were sold at 588p along with some July 550 puts at about 6p while July 600 calls were bought at 20p.
In general, as the share price falls, a profit will come from having sold the stock. But below 550p, the short puts may be assigned forcing the trader to buy back BAT shares.
If the shares rise above 600p, losses will be contained to some extent by exercising the calls to buy stock at 600p.

Amongst FTSE 100 index options, a volatility trade was executed when a dealer bought 1,300 August 500 calls at 31p while selling FTSE futures at 4753. The trade will make money on increased market volatility.
At 1300 GMT, cash FTSE was down 47.3 at 4,735.8 with June futures down 52 at 4,749 and September futures down 47 at 4,784.
